AK.reason: The corpus contains AS 08.40.210-08.40.490, which explicitly licenses and regulates mechanical administrators including those working with the Uniform Mechanical Code covering HVAC/heating/ventilation/air conditioning systems.

AL.reason: The corpus contains Alabama Code Chapter 34-31 which directly establishes and governs the State Board of Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors and sets out the full licensure/certification requirements for HVAC contractors.

AR.reason: The corpus is Arkansas Code Title 17 Chapter 33, which directly establishes the HVACR Licensing Board, defines HVACR work, and sets out licensing requirements for HVAC technicians and mechanical contractors.

CA.reason: This is California's Contractors State License Law (Business and Professions Code Chapter 9), which licenses all contractor classifications including HVAC/mechanical contractors under the specialty contractor provisions (e.g., Section 7058).

CT.reason: The corpus contains CT Secs. 20-341s through 20-341bb which explicitly define and require registration of mechanical contractors performing heating, piping and cooling work (HVAC), covering definitions, application, fees, enforcement, and penalties.

DE.reason: The corpus contains Delaware's Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners chapter, which explicitly licenses master HVACR technicians and contractors including sections on license requirements, qualifications, examinations, and enforcement.

FL.reason: The corpus covers Florida Chapter 489 which explicitly defines and licenses air-conditioning contractors and mechanical contractors (among other construction trades) including their board membership, qualifications, certification, and regulation.

GA.reason: The corpus is Georgia O.C.G.A. Chapter 43-14, which explicitly licenses and regulates conditioned air contractors (HVAC) including definitions, licensing requirements, examinations, and enforcement provisions.

HI.reason: Hawaii Chapter 444 licenses specialty contractors including HVAC/mechanical contractors, explicitly covers air conditioning work (CFC/refrigerant rules), and requires licenses for all specialty contracting trades.

IA.reason: Iowa Code Chapter 105 explicitly licenses HVAC contractors and mechanical professionals, defining HVAC, requiring licensure for HVAC work, and establishing the board, examinations, and disciplinary procedures for HVAC-refrigeration practitioners.

ID.reason: The corpus contains Idaho Code Title 54 Chapter 50, which is the dedicated HVAC licensing law establishing the Idaho HVAC board, certificate of competency requirements, classifications, examinations, and enforcement for heating, ventilation and air conditioning contractors and technicians.

LA.reason: The corpus covers Louisiana RS 37:2150 et seq., the State Licensing Board for Contractors chapter, which explicitly includes Mechanical as a major license classification (37:2156.1) and references mechanical construction throughout, directly licensing HVAC/mechanical contractors.

MD.reason: The corpus contains Maryland GBR Title 9A, which is the full licensure statute for the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, directly licensing HVAC contractors and technicians.

MI.reason: The corpus is Michigan's Skilled Trades Regulation Act (Act 407 of 2016, MCL 339.5101 et seq.), which is the statute that licenses and regulates mechanical contractors and HVAC technicians (among other skilled trades) in Michigan, as confirmed by the act's title, its reference to the former mechanical rules board (former 1984 PA 192), and the Michigan mechanical code definitions present in the text.

MN.reason: Chapter 326B covers construction codes and licensing in Minnesota, explicitly including the heating and ventilation industry (section 326B.07) and sections 326B.43 to 326B.59 which govern mechanical contractors and HVAC licensure, as confirmed by the citation list and deposit/fee references throughout the sampled text.

NC.reason: The corpus contains NC General Statutes Chapter 87 Article 2 (Plumbing and Heating Contractors), which explicitly licenses heating contractors including air conditioning (heating group number two and three) and defines the licensing board, examination, fees, and enforcement for HVAC/mechanical contractors.

NJ.reason: The corpus contains the full text of The State Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contracting License Law (N.J. P.L.2007, c.211), which directly licenses HVACR contractors in New Jersey.

NM.reason: The corpus is the New Mexico Construction Industries Licensing Act (Chapter 60, Article 13), which explicitly covers mechanical contractors and includes air conditioning and heating as licensed contracting activities under its jurisdiction.

NV.reason: NRS Chapter 624 is Nevada's contractor licensing law and explicitly covers specialty contractors including refrigeration and air-conditioning (HVAC) contractors, as shown in NRS 624.215 and 624.031 references to refrigeration, heating, and air-conditioning contractor classifications.

OH.reason: The corpus is Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4740, which explicitly establishes the Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board and licenses heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) contractors throughout its sections.

OK.reason: The corpus contains Oklahoma's Mechanical Licensing Act (59-1850.1 through 59-1850.17) which explicitly licenses mechanical contractors and journeymen performing HVAC, heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration work.

SC.reason: SC Code Chapter 40-11 explicitly licenses mechanical contractors including those performing heating, plumbing, or air conditioning work, and the board membership includes a contractor whose larger business is heating, plumbing, or air conditioning work.

TX.reason: The corpus is Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1302, the Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractor License Law, which directly licenses and regulates HVAC/air conditioning and refrigeration contractors and technicians.

UT.reason: Section 58-55-301 explicitly lists HVAC contractor as a license classification under the Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act, and the corpus contains the full licensure framework for that occupation.

VA.reason: The corpus explicitly covers HVAC contractor licensing as part of Virginia's contractor licensing chapter, including references to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning contractors in the definitions, board membership, and license classifications.

WA.reason: This corpus is Washington RCW chapter 18.27, the general contractor registration statute, which does not specifically license HVAC technicians or mechanical contractors as a distinct occupation.
